open_obligations: Check whether Smit et al. match compute budgets between MAD and self-consistency.
Note that Du et al.'s arithmetic and biography tasks are not in Smit et al.'s benchmark.
Check sensitivity to hyperparameters, which Smit et al. say MAD depends on.
in.other_title: Benchmark: multi-agent debate does not reliably beat self-consistency or ensembling
in.rationale: Du et al. note multi-agent debate is more computationally expensive than other prompting techniques. Smit et al. benchmark cost, time and accuracy and report MAD systems do not reliably beat self-consistency or ensembling, though tuned Multi-Persona can; datasets and protocols differ from Du et al.'s arithmetic and biography tasks.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: whether the extra cost of multi-agent debate buys accuracy over cheaper prompting, for GPT-3.5-turbo on seven QA datasets

text: The authors state that multiagent debate is more computationally expensive than other prompting techniques because it needs multiple generations and a debate procedure. They also observed that as debates got longer, models sometimes failed to process the whole debate and focused mainly on the most recent generations.
title: Debate is computationally costly and long debates exceed what models process
